overloadMerges.note: Fixed directions per the parameter table's arrow column: response is filled by the command ('out'), and headerNames/headerValues are read on input (request header names/values) and overwritten on output (response header names/values), so they are 'inout' rather than the mechanical parser's blanket 'in'.

params.name: url
params.description: URL to send the GET request to, e.g. http://[{user}:[{password}]@]host[:{port}][/{path}][?{queryString}].

params.name: response
params.description: Filled with the body of the server response; the variable's type (Text/Blob/Picture/Object/Collection) selects how the raw response is decoded/parsed.

params.name: headerNames
params.description: In: names of request headers to send. Out: overwritten with the names of headers returned by the server.

params.name: headerValues
params.description: In: values of request headers to send. Out: overwritten with the values of headers returned by the server.
If passed, keep the server connection alive after this call instead of closing it automatically.

overloadMerges.semanticRole: Sends an HTTP GET request to a URL and returns the server's response body plus response headers; the function result is the HTTP status code (0 if the connection itself failed).

constraints: If the response type doesn't match what the server actually returned (e.g. Object requested but response isn't parseable JSON), the mismatched case falls back: for Object, a 4D.Blob object is returned instead of a parse failure.
A return value of 0 indicates a network-level failure (DNS/unreachable server, not an HTTP error status) and an error is generated, interceptable via ON ERR CALL.
During HTTPS requests, the server certificate's authority is not checked by this command.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): HTTP client protocol: HTTP AUTHENTICATE / HTTP SET OPTION / HTTP SET CERTIFICATES FOLDER configure per-process client state -> HTTP Get or HTTP Request issues the request and consumes that state -> HTTP GET OPTION / HTTP Get certificates folder read back the currently active state.
